prerequisites: Linear algebra, differential and integral calculus, vector analysis, differential equations.
Basic concepts of electromagnetic fields and waves.

learning_outcomes.text: Analyze the propagation modes in a guided system.
Specify the characteristics of a guided system in terms of the propagation properties of its modes.
Manage the standards and specifications of commercial guided systems.
Analyze and characterize elements of a guided system using models based on network theory.
Analyze and specify different types of passive circuits according to their functionality.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Characterization of guided systems by N-port networks
Input/output impedances. Gains in two-port networks.
Introduction to Analysis of guided systems
Transmission lines. Effects of losses on basic parameters.
Propagation and dispersion. Modes in waveguides.
Waveguide specifications. Standards in guided systems.
Introduction to Passive microwave components in guided systems
Technological aspects of passive circuit implementation.
Two-port components: attenuators, phase shifters, impedance matching networks, isolators, orthomode transducers, transitions.

assessment_methods.method: Mid-semester test on basic and fundamental concepts (T1)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as (T1) x 0.15 + (T2) x 0.6 + (P1) x 0.25. A weighted score of 5 points or higher is required to pass the course. Students are considered "Not Presented" if their participation in evaluation activities is less than 50% of the total grade. In the extraordinary examination, the evaluation consists of a written exam covering all theoretical and practical content (75% theoretical, 25% practical). The practical evaluation can be replaced by the ordinary evaluation's practical grade upon student request, implicitly waiving the continuous evaluation grade.
